5.text: Meta launched its Muse AI agent, which topped ChatGPT’s early iOS downloads and lifted the stock, and unveiled a companion device plus expanded smart glasses and VR at its Connect event. Meta partnered with Shopify for AI shopping and checkout, signed retailers including Walmart, Sephora, and Best Buy, and said Muse will stay free for most users while taking small transaction fees.

6.text: Hyperscalers are spending roughly $1 trillion annually on AI infrastructure, pushing free cash flow down about $440 billion and forcing Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia to pay higher bond yields. Michael Burry warns of $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments and potential write-offs, while analysts flag negative cash flow, falling inference costs, and 2008-style debt risks.

7.text: A New Mexico jury found Meta misled consumers in the Cambridge Analytica case. Snap faces over 2,500 addiction lawsuits, and Meta and Singapore police dismantled scam networks, actioning 113,000 fraud-linked entities.

8.text: Meta shares rose about 33% in a month, closing at $744.10 and later $777.59, as AI monetization and ad momentum offset capex, debt, and cash-flow concerns. Analysts debated valuation and Meta Connect 2026 catalysts, with some seeing 40% upside and others warning against buying at highs.

9.text: Meta announced a transatlantic subsea cable project with 1-petabit-scale capacity to support its AI infrastructure. The company is betting its AI future on the cable's success.

10.text: Pinterest introduced visual search ads linking browsing to purchases. Snap released $2,195 AR glasses on September 16 amid demand concerns. AppLovin posted 53% year-over-year revenue growth but faces legal challenges, while Airbnb could add roughly 1 million rooms by year-end.

11.text: Meta's Muse AI agent hit No. 1 on Apple's U.S. free app chart, fueling bets that agentic AI will boost CPU demand. AMD jumped about 10% to a record and $1 trillion market cap, with Intel, Arm, and other chip stocks also rallying.

12.text: GE Vernova is compared with pre-revenue Oklo, and Constellation Energy is cited for its large nuclear fleet and rising power demand. EU-Philippines trade talks and a dividend ETF comparison (SCHD vs. RDVY) are also covered.
